name: Rabeprazole + Levosulpiride
meta: Rabeprazole Sodium: Proton pump inhibitor (PPI); Levosulpiride: Substituted benzamide prokinetic (D2 antagonist, 5-HT4 agonist)
Schedule H – prescription only; Levosulpiride: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: White to slightly yellowish-white solid (sodium salt), very soluble in water.

Rabeprazole Sodium: Its predominantly non-enzymatic metabolism makes it less affected by CYP2C19 polymorphism than other PPIs. First approval/introduction: Patented 1986; Japan 1997 (Eisai); Europe 1998; US FDA August 1999. Levosulpiride: The levorotatory enantiomer of sulpiride; widely used in Italy and India for dyspepsia, gastroparesis and as an antiemetic. First approval/introduction: Introduced in Italy in the 1980s (Ravizza).
Rabeprazole provides rapid acid suppression; levosulpiride enhances gastric emptying and has antiemetic and mild anxiolytic effects.

Rabeprazole Sodium Irreversibly inhibits gastric H+/K+-ATPase; activates rapidly over a wide pH range giving fast onset of acid suppression. Receptor / target profile: Covalently binds cysteine residues of H+/K+-ATPase via disulfide bonds; activates rapidly over a wide pH range.

Levosulpiride Levo-enantiomer of sulpiride; blocks central and peripheral D2 receptors and has mild 5-HT4 agonism, accelerating gastric emptying and improving dyspeptic symptoms; also antiemetic. Receptor / target profile: Selective D2 antagonist (central and peripheral) with moderate 5-HT4 agonism, enhancing gastric emptying.
Mainly non-enzymatic reduction to thioether; minor CYP2C19 and CYP3A4
Summary: Bioavailability ~52%; Tmax 2–5 h (enteric-coated). ~96% protein bound. Mainly non-enzymatic reduction (less CYP2C19-dependent). Half-life ~1 h.
Summary: Bioavailability ~30%; Tmax ~3 h. Low protein binding. Excreted largely unchanged in urine. Half-life ~7 h.
One capsule once daily before breakfast
Short-term use; monitor for EPS and hyperprolactinaemia, especially in elderly
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Use with caution in severe impairment.
High risk of EPS/tardive dyskinesia – avoid long-term.
Extrapyramidal symptoms and tardive dyskinesia, especially in elderly with prolonged use – limit duration
Rabeprazole Sodium: Supportive care. Levosulpiride: EPS, sedation; supportive care, anticholinergics for EPS.
Mearin et al., Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2004 – levosulpiride improved functional dyspepsia symptoms; component data support the combination.
Swallow whole – do not crush or chew
Do not use long-term without review
Report breast swelling or milk discharge
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
